name: Real-Time Multiplayer Arena
description: A server-authoritative arena with live rooms, combat, matchmaking, persistent results, and Elo ratings.
summary: Players can join manual rooms or enter rated matchmaking. The server owns simulation and final results, while clients predict and reconcile movement and recover after temporary disconnections.
architecture: Next.js hosts the lobby and match UI while Phaser renders the arena. Express and Socket.IO run authenticated rooms and authoritative game simulation. Redis stores live room and queue state; Prisma persists match history and rating changes to PostgreSQL at lifecycle boundaries.

capabilities.name: Authoritative combat
capabilities.description: Server-owned movement, projectile collisions, health, scores, and match completion.

capabilities.name: Matchmaking and recovery
capabilities.description: Match compatible players and recover queued or active sessions after refresh.

capabilities.name: Match history and ratings
capabilities.description: Persist results and apply atomic Elo updates for rated matches.

stack.usage: Pages expose registration, rooms, matchmaking, results, and match history.
Phaser renders the 2D arena, players, projectiles, camera, and HUD.
Express serves authentication and game-service endpoints.
Node.js runs server-owned movement, combat ticks, and lifecycle services.
Authenticated Socket.IO connections send player intents and authoritative snapshots.
Redis coordinates live rooms, queue membership, matchmaking, and recovery state.
Prisma writes completed matches and applies idempotent rated-match updates.
PostgreSQL persists authenticated player records, match results, and MMR history.
Shared TypeScript modules define networking payloads and game-domain types.

architectureConnections.description: The client sends input intent and reconciles server snapshots.
Room and matchmaking services maintain live state.
Match finalization persists standings and rating deltas.
